title: Top Escalations Analysis — Feb 2026 (Support + SRE + Docs)

content:
Redwood Inference — Customer Success / Support Ops
Doc: Top Escalations Analysis (Feb 2026)
Owner: Chris Osei (Product Ops)
Reviewers: Dev Patel (Support), Sean Gallagher (SRE), Elliot Price (Docs)
Last updated: 2026-02-22

Purpose
- One place to quantify top escalation drivers (volume + customer impact), list representative tickets, and propose validated workarounds + next fixes for the Feb–Mar “Escalation playbook + known-issues sprint”.
- This is not a perfect taxonomy; it’s a practical list for (a) playbook routing rules and (b) known-issues KB prioritization.

Data notes / definitions (quick)
- “Escalation” here = Support required engineering engagement (SRE, Runtime, Private Deployments, Security) OR customer impact significant enough that Support could not resolve from standard macros.
- Volume/Impact scoring is directional (Low/Med/High) based on Support weekly tags + oncall notes; we’ll replace with SLO-toolkit export once redwood/slo-toolkit#88 is live.
- Customer-identifying details intentionally omitted.

EXEC SUMMARY (Feb 2026)
- The top 4 recurring drivers for escalations are:
  1) Streaming disconnects (Hosted/Dedicated; often enterprise) — high pain + hard to distinguish client-side vs edge/runtime.
  2) Timeouts (Hosted; sometimes Dedicated) — mixed causes; needs better “what to collect” + dashboards.
  3) 429 throttling/quota misconfig (Self-serve) — high volume; mostly solvable via docs + SDK retry defaults + clearer quota UI.
  4) Private SSO/SAML login failures (Private/VPC) — lower volume but high severity due to access blockage + security implications.
- Common gap across all themes: missing request metadata in escalation handoff (request IDs, region, model, SDK version, retry policy, timestamps, streaming mode).
- Proposed sprint focus:
  - Publish 3 customer-safe KB pages (streaming reconnect guidance; 429 troubleshooting; Dedicated latency spikes) and 1 internal-only playbook page for Private SSO/SAML.
  - Add an “escalation required fields” checklist/lint (ENG-2842 + INT-1337) + incident-bot prompts (ENG-2843).
  - Add/refresh observability panels + runbook links for streaming/timeout rates (ENG-2844; observability-pack#301).


SHEET 1 — TOP DRIVERS TABLE (Spreadsheet-style)

Columns:
A Theme | B Volume (Feb) | C Impact | D Primary deployments | E Primary tiers | F Common symptoms | G Most likely root causes (current) | H What Support must collect (minimum) | I Current workaround (safe-to-share) | J Internal diagnostics / next steps | K Proposed fix (owner) | L Representative tickets | M Notes

1) Streaming disconnects / SSE drops
A: Streaming disconnects (SSE/Websocket) + partial outputs
B: High
C: High
D: Hosted API, Dedicated
E: Enterprise, Dedicated; some Self-serve spikes during launches
F: Customer sees “stream closed”, “connection reset”, truncated generation; retries sometimes duplicate tokens; higher rate in one region during peaks
G: Mixed: client/proxy idle timeouts; LB keepalive mismatch; runtime handling of client disconnects; intermittent edge timeouts; noisy network paths
H: Request IDs (3–5), org/project, region, model + pinned version, endpoint (chat/completions), streaming=true, timestamps (UTC), SDK + version, client timeout settings, proxy/CDN in path, sample code snippet (sanitized)
I: Recommend client-side reconnect with idempotency guard; increase client read timeout; implement exponential backoff with jitter; if pinned model version: test fallback/pin-to-latest minor; optionally switch region if elevated errors
J: Check streaming_disconnect_rate by region/model; correlate with gateway 499/504; pull edge logs for request IDs; verify customer proxy idle timeout; confirm runtime keepalive settings
K: (1) Observability improvements + dashboard panel (Allison Grant / SRE) — ENG-2844 / observability-pack#301
   (2) Runtime/edge stability fix (Mateo Alvarez / Runtime) — redwood#18742
   (3) Publish KB page + templates (Wei Chen + Priya Shah) — redwood-docs#642
L: SUP-4921; SUP-4925 (adjacent symptoms in eu-west during elevated 5xx)
M: Needs clear playbook rule: when streaming disconnect rate crosses threshold -> SRE page vs Support-managed guidance. Also needs a standard “do not promise” line re: exact ETA.

2) Timeouts (request timeouts / gateway 504 / client read timeout)
A: Timeouts (non-streaming and streaming) + “context deadline exceeded”
B: Med–High
C: High (when widespread); Medium (single account)
D: Hosted API; some Dedicated (peak)
E: Self-serve + Dedicated
F: 504s; slow first token; increased tail latency; customers raising timeouts from 30s to 120s with mixed results
G: Queueing under load; long prompts without batching; customer concurrency spikes exceeding quotas; regional capacity contention; model-specific latency regressions
H: Request IDs, prompt/input sizes (tokens), max_output_tokens, concurrency level, region/model, time window, whether retries enabled, latency p50/p95 from customer, any recent deploy/traffic change
I: Suggest higher client timeout for long generations + streaming; reduce max_output_tokens; enable streaming for better UX; implement retries only for safe errors; consider region failover during elevated errors
J: Check timeout_rate and queue_time; confirm whether throttling preceded timeouts; verify dedicated autoscaling status; compare to status page / incident threads
K: (1) Add timeout dashboard + runbook link surfaced to Support (SRE) — observability-pack#301
   (2) Docs: “timeouts & latency troubleshooting checklist” (Docs/DevEx) — redwood-docs#642
L: SUP-4925 (5xx + failover guidance); internal incident thread reference: Slack #incidents thread_1740068804_490015
M: Recommendation: explicitly separate “customer client timeout” vs “server timeout/504” in Support macros.

3) 429 throttling + quota / rate-limit misconfiguration
A: 429s / “rate limit exceeded” / “quota exceeded” confusion
B: High (largest by raw ticket count)
C: Medium (usually localized); High during product launches
D: Hosted API (self-serve)
E: Self-serve; occasionally high-growth teams nearing upgrade
F: Sudden burst of 429s after launch; retries worsen; customers assume it’s an outage; misunderstanding org vs project limits
G: Real rate limit enforcement; burst above per-route limit; misconfigured retries (no backoff); incorrect client parallelism; wrong API key/project usage
H: Org + project id, route, region, SDK + version, retry config, concurrency, approximate RPS/TPM, exact 429 payload/error code, whether multiple API keys used
I: Provide standard backoff w/ jitter; cap concurrency; respect Retry-After; validate correct project in dashboard; request temporary quota bump if warranted; upgrade path to Dedicated if sustained
J: Verify org/project limits in admin; check whether 429s correlate with 5xx/timeouts; confirm if customer on shared pool; ensure Support uses consistent “quota vs rate limit” language
K: (1) KB page: 429 troubleshooting + decision tree (Wei Chen / Priya Shah) — redwood-docs#642
   (2) SDK: improve default retry/backoff + clearer error messages (Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan) — redwood-sdk-python#519
   (3) Internal: macro/snippet library update (Support Ops) — INT-1338
L: SUP-4922; Slack #support thread_1739897755_558901
M: Strong deflection candidate. Add “what we can/can’t change immediately” section (e.g., instantaneous limit changes vs next billing/contract).

4) Private SSO / SAML login failures (IdP changes)
A: Private SSO/SAML breakage after IdP config updates
B: Low–Med
C: High (access blocked) + Security sensitivity
D: Private (VPC/on-prem)
E: Private/Enterprise
F: “Cannot login”; SAML assertion errors; redirects loop; audit logs not accessible; admin locked out
G: IdP cert rotation; attribute mapping changes; clock skew; incorrect ACS URL; RBAC mismatch; private control plane connectivity issue
H: Deployment type + version, IdP vendor, timestamps, SAML metadata (redacted), error screenshots (sanitized), private control-plane logs excerpt, recent changes, whether breakglass admin exists
I: Customer-safe: verify IdP metadata (cert/issuer) matches configured; validate ACS URL; test with breakglass admin; rollback to last known good IdP config if possible; schedule change window
J: Escalate to Security + Private Deployments early; check audit log pipeline; confirm if networking/egress to IdP endpoints is allowed; ensure restricted handling in Jira + Slack
K: (1) Internal-only runbook + comms template set (Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin + Vivek Kulkarni) — draft planned in Confluence
   (2) Add “restricted handling” reminder + required fields (Support Ops) — ENG-2842 + INT-1337
L: SUP-4923
M: Needs clear severity guidance: typically Sev1/Sev2 depending on number of users impacted and whether breakglass exists. Avoid asking for full SAML assertions in plain text.

5) Dedicated latency spikes (noisy neighbor / capacity contention)
A: Dedicated latency spikes during peak hours
B: Med
C: High (SLA risk)
D: Dedicated
E: Dedicated/Enterprise
F: p95 latency spikes; slow first token; throughput drops; customer sees intermittent timeouts; often time-of-day correlated
G: Capacity saturation; autoscaling policy too conservative; workload mix changes; routing/fallback policy; noisy-neighbor suspicion even within semi-isolated pools
H: Dedicated cluster ID, region, model, time window, baseline p50/p95, concurrency, autoscaling settings, recent workload change, dashboards screenshots
I: Customer-safe: verify autoscaling knobs; temporarily overprovision; adjust max concurrency; enable fallback to compatible model variant if allowed; schedule load test
J: Check GPU utilization, queue depth, batch size distribution; confirm isolation guarantees; compare to other tenants; evaluate whether resize needed
K: (1) Runbook refresh + alert tuning to reduce false pages (Tomáš Novák / SRE) — ENG-2845
   (2) KB page (customer-safe diagnostics + knobs) (Kira Thompson / Priya Shah) — redwood-docs#642
L: SUP-4924
M: Important to align comms expectations: we can mitigate quickly, but “root cause” may require deeper capacity planning.


SHEET 2 — “FASTEST DEFLECTION” CANDIDATES (if KB + SDK improvements ship)

Columns: Theme | Why it escalates today | What changes would deflect | Target deliverable | Owner | ETA
- 429 throttling/quota: escalates due to confusion + poor retry defaults | Improve docs + SDK errors/backoff + macro | KB + sdk PR | Wei / Monica / Ibrahim | Feb–Mar
- Streaming disconnects: escalates due to ambiguous blame + missing metadata | KB reconnect guidance + better dashboard panels + required fields | KB + observability | Priya / Allison | Feb–Mar
- Timeouts: escalates due to missing “timeouts checklist” + unclear client vs server | KB checklist + updated Support macros | Docs + Support Ops | Elliot / Owen | Mar


SHEET 3 — “GAPS / OPEN QUESTIONS” (to finalize playbook v2)

1) After-hours thresholds
- Question: When do we page SRE for customer-reported streaming disconnects if we don’t yet see a global metric spike?
- Proposal (draft): Page SRE if enterprise/dedicated AND (a) multiple regions, or (b) repeated within 30 min with ≥X% failure in customer samples, or (c) any correlated increase in 5xx/timeout dashboards.
- Owner: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (needs paging hygiene alignment)

2) Severity mapping consistency
- Question: For Private SSO, do we treat “admin locked out” as Sev1 automatically?
- Proposal: Yes unless breakglass admin confirmed working; otherwise Sev2 with immediate Security/Private engagement.
- Owner: Naomi Feldman + Dev Patel

3) Required fields enforcement
- Gap: Support escalations missing request IDs + timestamps, causing long MTTA.
- Action: Add escalation required field checklist + automation prompts.
- Owners: ENG-2842 (Support workflow), ENG-2843 (incident-bot), INT-1337 (Jira fields)


NEXT STEPS (Feb 22 → Mar rollout)
- Confirm top 4 known-issues KB pages and owners; publish internal first, then safe-to-share excerpts.
- Lock escalation thresholds + paging rules in Confluence Escalation Playbook v2.
- Run a 2-week pilot (Support + SRE): measure time-to-ack, time-to-mitigation, # of pages, and deflection rate.
